for LINK holders: What makes you think LINK will actually pump by itself?

Open thread • Replies: 31 • Updated: 2026-09-21 20:33 UTC

OP

Serious question for LINK holders:

What makes you think LINK will actually pump by itself? Over the last 5 years, LINK has performed pretty much in line with the general altcoin market. Blue line is the total crypto market excluding BTC, compared against LINK on the regular chart.

Most of the things people used to speculate about Chainlink have already happened, so you could argue they're already priced in.

>Chainlink becomes the standard oracle
Already happened. Priced in.

>Integrations across the entire crypto ecosystem, including institutions like DTCC and SWIFT
Already happened. Priced in.

>Sergey gets invited to government events and even appears with Trump
Already happened. Priced in.

I'm a LINK holder myself and I think Chainlink is, and will continue to be, a very successful project. But if I'm being realistic, I don't see why the LINK token itself should suddenly have some massive independent pump just because of more partnerships or good news.

In 2020/2021, LINK had a huge narrative behind it. Crypto was flooded with new people, influencers were shilling everything, and tons of people were buying whatever sounded cool without really understanding it. That kind of retail hype doesn't really exist right now unless something turns into a mainstream meme or gets pushed by someone like Elon, Trump, etc.

So I don't have huge expectations for LINK to pull another independent 2020 style run.

I see it more as crypto in general pumping for whatever reason, with LINK being one of the relatively "safe" large cap bets, similar to ETH or BTC, rather than something that's going to massively outperform the rest of the market on its own.

What are your thoughts?

Really simple, s curve of adoption. If you look at the 2020 portion of the chart, link wasn't following or keeping pace with alts, it was leading the market heavily and obliterating it. That's the first portion of the s curve, the early adopters. After that point it was clear all the things it would do had years of work before they could be enacted in the real world.

From there, absolutely it just followed the market (which is why its so obnoxious when fuddies spam the board 24/7 with shit like pumps the least dumps the most, it has just been flowing with the market over that period).

This year, all of those partnerships are starting to enter into production, swift/dtcc are fully mask-off. The only things left are a few more regulatory matters and full implementation of staking. Compared to the top of the market, relatively few people still hold chainlink (the peak at this point is like 900,000 wallets). For perspective, that's about 0.01% of the entire world's population that holds link at most, and likely less than that because many people have multiple wallets.

Now granted, what's going to actually make link explode is usage of the token separate from speculatory holders. But that just shows even in terms of speculation, the ceiling from just this point is still massive. For comparisons sake, there are over 200 million unique wallets with ETH, that's 200x the amount that hold link.

The only thing left is for the next phase of the s curve to actually take off. So unless you're just bearish on crypto in general (a fair stance admittedly), link is perfectly positioned to do what it did in 2020 all over again but to a far greater degree this time. Just look at the setup, at this point the general market won't even get excited until link hits triple digits, possibly mid triple digits, which means a 4 digit run is easily possible. And this is on top of the implications of what actual staking integration will look like.

Instead its being treated simply as another long term supply.

>and why would that happen? they've already confirmed no banks will actually buy or hold the token.
Are you genuinely someone new who stumbled on /biz/ and curious about chainlink and their staking model? The tl;dr is banks won't even have to directly interact with the token, the conversions will all happen on the backend, but nodes will have to (eventually) stake tokens to prove they can be trusted/secure. Staking is a chicken and egg scenario, the network needs enough demand to justify true staking (otherwise nodes will prefer to just sell their tokens as they go), but in order to get that demand, you need legitimate customers who actually want security (swift/dtcc/tradfi etc). This is where you would jump off the train, if you didn't believe this problem could be solved. >and? there's 50 million altcoins that people spread liquidity over.
As pointed out in OP, altcoin market is pumping less and less over time. Shitcoin casino is a dying usecase, and that money is going to continue to consolidate into the few legitimate projects, no different than the dotcom boom seeing liquidity flow into the companies that survived it 25 years ago.
